tasks.title: The Evolution of the Workweek
paras: According to anthropologists, people in preindustrial societies spent 3 to 4 hours per day or about 20 hours per week doing the work necessary for life. Modern comparisons of the amount of work performed per week, however, begin with the Industrial Revolution (1760–1840) when 10- to 12-hour workdays with six workdays per week were the norm.

Even with extensive time devoted to work, both incomes and standards of living were low. As incomes rose near the end of the Industrial Revolution, it became increasingly common to treat Saturday afternoons as a half-day holiday.

In the United States, the first third of the twentieth century saw the workweek move from 60 hours per week to just under 50 hours by the start of the 1930s. In 1914 Henry Ford reduced daily work hours at his automobile plants from 9 to 8. In 1926 he announced that his factories would close for the entire day on Saturday.

The Depression years of the 1930's brought with them the notion of job sharing to spread available work around; the workweek dropped to a modern low for the United States of 35 hours.In 1938 the Fair Labor Standards Act mandated a weekly maximum of 40 hours to begin in 1940, and since that time the 8-hour day, 5-day workweek has been the standard in the United States.

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly discuss?

options.A: Why people in preindustrial societies worked few hours per week
options.B: Changes that have occurred in the number of hours that people work per week
options.C: A comparison of the number of hours worked per year in several industries
options.D: Working conditions during the Industrial Revolution

questions.analysis: 题型：主旨题 原文定位： 通读全文结构，四段依时间顺序从 preindustrial → industrial → 20世纪改革，聚焦工时变迁。 正确答案分析： 文章围绕“人们每周工作时间的变化”展开，讲述从前工业时代的轻劳动到工业革命的高强度劳动，再到20世纪工时的缩减和法律规定，逻辑线条明确。 选项分析： A. 虽提到 preindustrial 社会，但不是文章主线； C. 并未涉及多个行业的每年工时对比； D. 工业革命是背景，不是全篇重点。

questions.stem: Compared to preindustrial times, the number of hours in the workweek in the nineteenth
questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位： 第1段：“people in preindustrial societies... about 20 hours per week”；“...Industrial Revolution... 10- to 12-hour workdays with six workdays per week...” 正确答案分析： 前后对比显示从每周20小时提升至每周60–72小时，显著上升。 选项分析： A、B、C 都与文中数据不符。

questions.stem: The word "norm" in the text is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 题型：词汇题 原文定位： 第1段：“...six workdays per week were the norm.” 正确答案分析： “norm”在这里表示“通常的情况”，与“standard（常规做法）”语义一致。 选项分析： A minimum（最低）不符语境；B example（例子）太泛；C possibility（可能性）不搭配。

questions.stem: What is one reason for the change in the length of the workweek for the average worker in the United States during the 1930's?

options.A: Several people sometimes shared a single job.
options.B: Labor strikes in several countries influenced labor policy in the United States.
options.C: Several corporations increased the length of the workweek.
options.D: The United States government instituted a 35-hour workweek.

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位： 第4段：“...the notion of job sharing to spread available work around...” 正确答案分析： “大萧条”导致失业，采用“工作共享”以缩短每人工时并扩大就业机会。 选项分析： B 无关，美国当时未受外国罢工影响； C 与文意相反； D 政府设定是40小时，不是35小时。

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence?

options.A: The Fair Labor Standards Act set the 8-hour workday in 1938, but it was never implemented.
options.B: A 40-hour weekly work limit was established by law in 1938 to begin in 1940, and since then, the 8-hour day, 5-day workweek has been the usual schedule in the U.S.
options.C: The workweek in the United States became 8 hours per day and 5 days per week only after the year 2000.
options.D: In 1940, a law was passed allowing workers to choose their own work hours.

questions.analysis: 题型：句子简化题 原文定位： 第4段：“In 1938 the Fair Labor Standards Act mandated a weekly maximum of 40 hours to begin in 1940...” 正确答案分析： 该句说明法律设定40小时工时上限，自1940年起生效，之后形成8小时×5天的工作制度。 选项分析： A 错误地说“从未实施”；C 错误时间；D 曲解为“工人可自由选择时间”。
